name: Install localized floor protection around spray work area
notes: SF/hr. Canvas drop cloths around discrete element work areas. Floor-level work — no overhead penalty. Localized protection (not full room). Spray only.

name: Install perimeter floor protection near work area
notes: SF/hr. Drop cloth runners near element work areas. Floor-level work. Brush only.

name: Mask wall surfaces adjacent to elements
notes: LF/hr. Tape + masking paper/film at beam-wall, column-wall, and mantel-wall junctions. Working at various heights. Spray only.

name: Mask ceiling fixtures near beam spray work
notes: EA/hr. Tape and plastic bag over each ceiling fixture. Overhead work near beam spray zone. Spray only.

name: Dust and clean all element surfaces
notes: Per room. Tack cloth or damp wipe all beam, column, and mantel surfaces. Mixed heights — beams overhead, columns full-height, mantels wall-height. Time scales with element count but FIXED per room is reasonable for typical 1-3 elements per room.

name: Sand beam surfaces per substrate and state
notes: LF/hr. Overhead work on ceiling-mounted beams. 3 exposed faces (bottom + 2 sides). SS_BARE: 150-220 grit, ~0.85x of equivalent trim rates. SS_PRIMED_FACTORY: lighter scuff sand. Apply beam_profile complexity modifier.

name: Sand column surfaces per substrate and state
notes: EA/hr. Based on 8ft square_smooth column (baseline). 4 flat faces, full height — ladder needed for upper portion. Fluted columns: flexible sanding sponge in channels. Apply column_type complexity modifier.

name: Sand mantel surfaces per substrate and state
notes: EA/hr. Based on standard_surround (baseline). Shelf, legs/pilasters, and surround molding. Wall height (H1). Detail profiles require flexible sanding approach. Apply mantel_type complexity modifier.

name: Fill fastener holes and defects on beams
notes: LF/hr. qt_scaled. Overhead work. Beam miters and assembly fasteners. Apply beam_profile complexity modifier.

name: Caulk beam-to-structure junctions
notes: LF/hr. Beam-to-ceiling junction full length (both sides = ~2 LF caulk per 1 LF beam), plus miter joints at beam intersections. Overhead work. Use flexible painter's caulk for movement-prone junctions. Apply beam_profile modifier.

name: Caulk column-to-structure junctions
notes: EA/hr. Based on 8ft square_smooth column. Top perimeter + bottom perimeter + back edge (wall-mounted). Significant caulk per column — full perimeter at top and bottom is ~8 LF+ each. Apply column_type modifier.

name: Caulk mantel-to-wall junctions
notes: EA/hr. Based on standard_surround. Mantel-to-wall all contact edges, shelf-to-leg joints, leg-to-wall junctions. full_assembly has significantly more junction LF (1.50x modifier). Apply mantel_type modifier.

name: Seal MDF cut/routed edges (solvent-based)
notes: Per room. All MDF elements — beam miters, column panel joints, mantel shelf edges, leg edges. Shellac/oil-based sealer applied by small brush to each cut/routed edge. MANDATORY step 1 of MDF two-step prime. NON-NEGOTIABLE. Conditional: substrate=MDF AND substrate_state=SS_BARE. Time depends on element count and complexity.

name: Prime beam surfaces
notes: LF/hr. Full primer coat, multi-angle passes for 3-sided coverage. Overhead work ~0.85x of equivalent trim rates. Primer type driven by substrate (MDF step 2 latex, FJP stain-block, hardwood tannin-block, softwood acrylic). Apply beam_profile modifier.

name: Prime column surfaces
notes: EA/hr. Based on 8ft square_smooth column. Full coat top-to-bottom. Height modifier applies — upper portion requires ladder. Apply column_type modifier.

name: Prime mantel surfaces
notes: EA/hr. Based on standard_surround. Shelf, legs/pilasters, surround detail. Wall height (H1 typical). Apply mantel_type modifier.

name: Spray finish coat on beams
notes: LF/hr. Multiple angle spray passes for 3-sided beam coverage. Bottom face first (overhead), then side faces. Lighter coats on bottom to prevent sags. Overhead factor ~0.85x of equiv. trim rate baked in. Apply beam_profile modifier.

name: Spray finish coat on columns
notes: EA/hr. Based on 8ft square_smooth column. Rotate around column with consistent overlap, top-to-bottom. Fluted: angle spray into channels. Round: continuous rotation. Thin coats on vertical faces. Apply column_type modifier. Height modifier stacks.

name: Spray finish coat on mantels
notes: EA/hr. Based on standard_surround. Detail profiles first (recessed areas, molding), then flat faces (shelf top, leg fronts). Wall height. Apply mantel_type modifier.

name: Brush finish coat on beams
notes: LF/hr. Work face-by-face. Bottom (overhead) hardest — load brush lighter. Apply, tip once, walk away (FFD SS15.3.1). Ornate profiles require detail brush. Overhead factor ~0.85x baked in. Apply beam_profile modifier.

name: Brush finish coat on columns
notes: EA/hr. Based on 8ft square_smooth column. Square: Roll and Tip on flat faces per FFD SS15.6. Round/fluted: brush only, follow profile. Top-to-bottom. Apply column_type modifier. Height modifier stacks.

name: Brush finish coat on mantels
notes: EA/hr. Based on standard_surround. Shelf: Roll and Tip on flat top. Legs/pilasters: brush with grain. Molding detail: small angled brush. Apply, tip once, walk away. Apply mantel_type modifier.

notes: Per interstage cycle. qt_scaled. Touch-up patched areas to match surrounding finish before next full coat.

name: Tack cloth all element surfaces
notes: Per interstage cycle. Remove all sanding dust with tack cloth. Cover every surface — work into profile detail. Mixed heights.

name: Final quality inspection of all elements
notes: Per room. qt_scaled. Inspect all elements. Key checkpoints: beam underside sags, column run marks, mantel shelf edge drips, caulk line quality, sheen uniformity, profile detail coverage. QT5: angled light on all faces, zero tolerance.

name: Touch-up defects found during final inspection
notes: Per room. qt_scaled. Correct remaining defects, feather into surrounding finish. QT5 may require full additional coat if defects are widespread.

name: Remove wall adjacent masking
notes: LF/hr. Score tape edge before removal, pull at 45-degree angle. Faster than setup (80 LF/hr) — removal is simpler. Spray only.

name: Remove fixture masking
notes: EA/hr. Remove tape and plastic from ceiling fixtures. Clean adhesive residue. Faster than setup. Spray only.

name: Remove floor protection
notes: SF/hr. Floor-level work. Fold canvas/paper inward to contain debris. Covers both workzone (spray) and perimeter (brush) removal.

name: Vacuum work area
notes: SF/hr. Floor-level work. Vacuum floor area after protection removal.

name: Clean tools and equipment
notes: Per session. Clean brushes, spray equipment, dispose of consumables. Water cleanup for waterborne products. Solvent cleanup for shellac-based MDF edge sealer residue.

name: Install localized floor protection around spray work area and sawhorse zone
notes: SF/hr. Canvas drop cloths at built-in base and sawhorse area. Floor-level work. Localized — not full room. Spray only.

name: Install perimeter floor protection at built-in base
notes: SF/hr. Drop cloth runners at built-in base. Floor-level work. Brush only.

name: Mask wall surfaces adjacent to built-in
notes: LF/hr. Tape + masking paper/film at built-in-to-wall junctions (sides and top). Spray only.

name: Mask ceiling fixtures near spray work area
notes: EA/hr. Tape and plastic bag over each ceiling fixture. Spray only.

name: Remove all hardware from built-in unit
notes: EA/hr (hardware pieces). Remove hinges, knobs, pulls, catches, shelf pins. Bag and tag by opening number. ~3 min per piece including labeling. Typically 2-3 hardware pieces per door.

name: Remove doors and drawer fronts for flat painting
notes: EA/hr (doors/drawers). Unhinge, label position, set on sawhorses. ~7-8 min per door including labeling and sawhorse setup. Glass doors excluded.

name: Dust and clean all built-in surfaces
notes: Per room. Tack cloth or damp wipe all surfaces — inside compartments, face frames, removed doors. Built-in interiors trap construction dust in corners and shelf dados. More thorough than arch element due to enclosed compartments.

name: Sand interior compartment surfaces by opening tier
notes: EA/hr by tier. Sand all interior surfaces per opening (sides, top, bottom, back, shelves). Rigid block on flat shelf faces. Flexible sponge for inside corners and dado joints. Deep openings require reaching into compartments. Apply depth/detail/access modifiers.

name: Sand door/drawer front surfaces
notes: EA/hr. Flat on sawhorses — easy access. Rigid block on flat faces. Edge sanding for profiles. SS_PRIMED_FACTORY: lighter scuff sand only.

name: Fill fastener holes and defects in openings
notes: EA/hr by tier and QT. qt_scaled. High fastener density — shelves, dividers, back panels, face frames all nailed/screwed. NC overfill-sand-flush method. Apply depth/detail/access modifiers.

name: Fill fastener holes and defects on doors/drawers
notes: EA/hr. qt_scaled. Flat on sawhorses — easy access. Fill hinge screw holes, pull/knob fastener holes. Fewer holes than carcass openings.

name: Caulk built-in-to-wall junctions and interior joints
notes: Per room. Perimeter caulk at built-in-to-wall junction + visible interior shelf-to-side joints + face frame-to-carcass joints. Time scales with built-in size and detail level. Tooled caulk lines — higher quality expectation than closet shelving.

name: Seal MDF cut/routed edges (solvent-based)
notes: Per room. All MDF cut/routed edges inside openings and on door/drawer edges. Shelf dado joints, face frame rabbets, divider joints, back panel rabbets, door edges. Built-in MDF has very high edge density — more edges than arch element.

name: Prime interior compartment surfaces by opening tier
notes: EA/hr by tier. Full primer coat on all interior surfaces. Primer type substrate-driven (MDF step 2 latex, FJP stain-block, hardwood tannin-block, softwood acrylic). Apply depth/detail/access modifiers. Conditional: SS_BARE only.

name: Prime door/drawer fronts flat on sawhorses
notes: EA/hr. Flat orientation — gravity-assisted leveling. Face and edges. Same substrate-driven primer as carcass. Easy access on sawhorses. Conditional: SS_BARE only.

name: Spray finish coat on opening interiors
notes: EA/hr by tier. Spray reaches all interior surfaces uniformly. Light coats to prevent buildup on vertical interior surfaces. Overspray inside enclosed compartments. Apply depth/detail/access modifiers. Spray only.

name: Brush finish coat on opening interiors
notes: EA/hr by tier. Brush/mini roller combination. Apply, tip once, walk away (FFD SS15.3.1). 2-minute window. Work shelf-by-shelf. Apply depth/detail/access modifiers. Brush only.

name: Spray finish coat on door/drawer fronts
notes: EA/hr. Flat on sawhorses — gravity-assisted leveling. Spray face then edges. Light even coats. ~6 min per door. Spray only.

name: Brush finish coat on door/drawer fronts
notes: EA/hr. Flat on sawhorses. Roll and Tip method (FFD SS15.6) on flat face — mini roller to apply, brush to tip. Edges with angled sash brush. ~12 min per door. Flat orientation eliminates sag risk. Brush only.

name: Clean work area between coats
notes: Per interstage cycle. Remove dust and debris from floor protection and sawhorse area. Clear dust from inside compartments.

notes: Per interstage cycle. qt_scaled. Inspect openings and doors in one pass. QT3: quick scan for obvious defects. QT4: systematic 3-foot inspection, light inside compartments, mark defects. QT5: lighted critical inspection at arm's length, zero tolerance. Use flashlight inside deep compartments. Check shelf faces for brush marks, inside corners for runs, door fronts for leveling.

name: Sand between coats on opening interiors
notes: EA/hr by tier and QT. qt_scaled. Per interstage cycle. Rigid block on flat shelf faces (FFD SS15.4.1). Flexible sponge for inside corners and dado joints. Good lighting essential inside deep compartments. Apply depth/detail/access modifiers.

name: Sand between coats on door/drawer fronts
notes: EA/hr. qt_scaled. Per interstage cycle. Flat on sawhorses — easy access. Rigid block on flat face. Profile edges with flexible approach.

name: Floor Protection Setup (Brush/Roll)
notes: Drop cloth placement per frame location. ~4 min per frame. Simpler setup than door slab (no door swing).

name: Floor Protection Setup (Spray)
notes: Rosin paper 8ft radius per frame opening. ~7-8 min per frame.

name: Wall Adjacent Protection (Spray)
notes: Mask wall adjacent to frame opening. ~6 min per frame (both sides of opening).

name: Mask Door Hardware (Hinges + Strike Plate)
notes: Mask 3 hinge leaves + strike plate. ~6 min per frame.

name: Inspect Frame Surface
notes: Visual inspection per frame set (3 jambs + stop). QT2: Quick glance at 8-10 ft ~1 min (upper range ~40/hr). QT3: Note obvious defects ~2 min. QT4: Systematic at 3 ft ~3 min. QT5: Critical with light ~4 min. Faster than door slab (simpler geometry).

name: Sand Frame Surface (Prep)
notes: Scuff sand all jamb and stop surfaces. QT2: Light scuff 180 grit quick pass ~4 min (upper range ~15/hr). QT3: Uniform scratch pattern ~5 min. QT4+: Thorough ~6-7 min. Less surface area than door slab.

name: Fill Stop Nail Holes
notes: Fill nail holes in door stop. ~6-8 holes per frame typical. QT2: Obvious/large holes only ~2 min (upper range ~25/hr). QT3: Obvious holes ~3 min. QT4: All visible ~4 min. QT5: Every hole ~5 min.

name: Sand Filled Areas
notes: Sand filler spots smooth. ~2 min per frame.

name: Caulk Frame-to-Casing Gap
notes: Caulk gap between frame and casing. ~6 min per frame (both sides of jambs + head).

name: Clean Sanding Dust
notes: Tack cloth wipe all frame surfaces. ~1.5 min per frame.

name: Spray Primer on Frame
notes: Airless spray primer coat on frame set. ~4 min per frame. Faster than slab (simpler geometry).

name: Brush Primer on Frame
notes: Brush primer coat on frame set. ~7-8 min per frame. Brush is ~1.2x spray time.

name: Inspect Coat (Interstage)
notes: Visual inspection between coats. QT2: Quick glance for failures only ~1 min (upper range ~40/hr). QT3: Quick ~1.5 min. QT4: Systematic ~2.5 min. QT5: Critical ~3.5 min.

name: Light Sand Between Coats
notes: QT2: Quick scuff 180 single pass ~1.5 min (upper range ~15/hr), ~20% faster than QT3. QT3: Spot sand ~2 min. QT4: Full sand 220 ~5 min. QT5: Thorough 320 ~6 min per frame.

name: Patch/Repair Defects (Interstage)
notes: Spot patch defects found during interstage inspection. QT2: Skip unless coating failure risk ~0.5 min (upper range). QT3: Glaring defects ~2 min. QT4: All marked ~3 min. QT5: All defects ~4 min. QT2 saves ~5-10 min per frame on interstage repair.

name: Clean Sanding Dust (Interstage)
notes: Tack cloth wipe between coats. ~1.5 min per frame.

name: Spray Finish Coat on Frame
notes: Airless spray finish coat on frame set. ~5 min per frame. Slightly slower than primer for quality finish.

name: Brush Finish Coat on Frame
notes: Brush finish coat on frame set. ~10 min per frame. Work systematically: head → jambs → stop.

name: Roll and Tip Finish Coat on Frame
notes: Roll and Tip method: roller deposits, brush tips. ~8-9 min per frame. Slightly faster than brush-only.

name: Touch Up Mortise Areas
notes: Touch up 3 hinge mortises + 1 strike mortise per frame. ~4 min per frame. Bundled per-frame, not per-hinge.

name: Final Frame Inspection
notes: Final inspection per frame. QT2: Quick glance at 8-10 ft, obvious failures only ~1 min (upper range ~40/hr). QT3: 6 ft ~1.5 min. QT4: 3 ft ~2.5 min. QT5: Arm's length ~3.5 min. Minor brush marks/orange peel acceptable at QT2.

name: Remove Hardware Masking
notes: Remove masking tape from hinges and strike plate. ~3 min per frame.

name: Floor Protection Teardown
notes: Remove floor protection per frame location. ~2.5 min per frame.

name: Wall Protection Teardown
notes: Remove wall masking. ~3 min per frame.

name: Clean Tools
notes: Fixed time: ~30-45 min per session regardless of frame count. Modeled as flat allowance.

name: Floor Protection Setup
notes: Drop cloth placement per door location. ~5 min per door. Shared across doors in same room.

name: Spray Protection Setup
notes: Mask walls around door opening + extend floor protection. ~10 min per door.

name: Remove Door Hardware
notes: Remove lockset + 3 hinges, bag and label. ~20 min per door. Per Doors Doctrine §10.

name: Mask Door Hardware
notes: Mask 3 hinges (~5 min each) + lockset (~5 min). ~20 min per door total.

name: Inspect Door Surface
notes: Visual inspection per door side. QT3 (MINIMUM): ~3 min, note obvious defects. QT4: ~4 min, systematic inspection. QT5: ~5 min, critical raking light. QT2 NOT APPLICABLE for doors.

name: Sand Door Surface (Prep)
notes: Scuff sand factory primer or full sand bare wood. QT3 (MINIMUM): ~7 min scuff sand. QT4: ~8 min full sand 180. QT5: ~10 min thorough 150-180. QT2 NOT APPLICABLE for doors.

name: Fill Fastener Holes
notes: Fill nail holes. QT3 (MINIMUM): ~2 min, obvious holes. QT4: ~2 min, all visible. QT5: ~3 min, every hole. QT2 NOT APPLICABLE for doors.

name: Sand Filled Areas
notes: Sand filler spots. QT3 (MINIMUM): ~2 min, knock down ridges. QT4: ~2 min, flush. QT5: ~3 min, invisible. QT2 NOT APPLICABLE for doors.

name: Seal MDF Edges
notes: Brush shellac on exposed MDF edges. ~4 min per side (edges assigned to that side).

name: Clean Sanding Dust
notes: Tack cloth wipe. ~2 min per side.

name: Spray Primer on Door
notes: Airless spray primer coat per door side. ~5 min per side including edges. Production pace.

name: Brush Primer on Door
notes: Brush primer coat per door side. ~12 min per side. Slower than spray.

name: Inspect Coat (Interstage)
notes: Visual inspection between coats. QT3 (MINIMUM): quick glance ~2 min. QT4: systematic ~4 min. QT5: critical ~5 min. QT2 NOT APPLICABLE for doors.

name: Light Sand Between Coats
notes: QT3 (MINIMUM): spot sand ~3 min. QT4: full sand 220 ~8 min. QT5: thorough 320 ~10 min per side. QT2 NOT APPLICABLE for doors.

name: Patch/Repair Defects (Interstage)
notes: Spot patch defects. QT3 (MINIMUM): ~2 min, glaring defects only. QT4: ~3 min, all marked. QT5: ~5 min, every defect. QT2 NOT APPLICABLE for doors.

name: Clean Sanding Dust (Interstage)
notes: Tack cloth wipe between coats. ~2 min per side.

name: Spray Finish Coat on Door
notes: Airless spray finish coat per door side. ~6 min per side. Slightly slower than primer for quality finish. Flush door baseline.

name: Brush Finish Coat on Door
notes: Brush finish coat per door side. ~15 min per side. Flush door baseline.

name: Mask Glass Panes (French)
notes: Mask one glass pane — tape all 4 edges precisely. ~6 min per pane.

name: Remove Glass Masking (French)
notes: Remove masking from one glass pane. ~3 min per pane.

name: Final Door Inspection
notes: Final inspection per door side. QT3 (MINIMUM): ~2 min, quick glance at 6 ft. QT4: ~4 min, systematic at 3 ft. QT5: ~5 min, critical arm's length. QT2 NOT APPLICABLE for doors.

name: Reinstall Door Hardware
notes: Reinstall lockset + hinges, verify door operation. ~15 min per door. Per Doors Doctrine §10.

name: Remove Hardware Masking
notes: Remove masking tape from hinges and hardware. ~5 min per door.

name: Floor Protection Teardown
notes: Remove floor protection per door location. ~3 min per door.

name: Clean Tools
notes: Fixed time: ~30-45 min per session regardless of door count. Modeled as flat allowance.

name: Inspect Ceiling Surface

QT2 uses this same task but at faster pace (~1600 SF/hr) with quick walk-through and major defects only. QT4 uses separate TSK_CEIL_INSPECT_QT4 task with comprehensive inspection.

name: Inspect Ceiling Surface (Premium)
notes: Detailed ceiling inspection with raking work light. ~15% slower than wall QT4 inspection (1000 SF/hr) due to overhead angle.

name: Vacuum Ceiling Drywall Dust

notes: Careful ceiling brush cut-in for crisp straight line. ~13% slower than wall QT4 cut-in (75 LF/hr) due to overhead position.

name: Roll Primer on Ceiling

name: Roll Primer on Textured Ceiling
notes: Textured ceiling surface with 3/4-inch nap roller overhead. ~15% slower than wall textured rolling (275 SF/hr).

name: Roll Primer on Ceiling (Premium)
notes: Premium ceiling roller application. ~15% slower than wall QT4 rolling (275 SF/hr). Overhead fatigue + quality attention.

name: Mask Adjacent Surfaces for Ceiling Spray
notes: Apply tape and paper to wall tops for ceiling spray masking. ~13% slower than wall masking (150 LF/hr) — working at ceiling line is overhead reach.

name: Floor Protection Setup (Full Room)
notes: Full room floor coverage with rosin paper or plastic. Tape seams. Larger scope than wall spray perimeter protection.

name: Floor Protection Teardown
notes: Fold and remove floor protection. Faster than setup.

name: Spray Primer on Ceiling
notes: Airless spray upward at proper mil thickness. ~17% slower than wall spray (600 SF/hr) due to overhead position, overspray management, and fatigue.

name: Spray Primer on Ceiling (Premium)

name: Spray Ceiling Primer (No Backroll)

name: Backroll Sprayed Ceiling Primer

notes: Runner-style drop cloths along window perimeter (brush method) or full radial coverage (spray method). ~12 sec per SF. Same rate as trim floor protection. Spray method uses PS_PROTECT_SF.FLOOR_8FT_RADIUS instead.

name: Glass Masking
notes: MANDATORY — all methods, all tiers. Largest single protection task for window painting.

name: Hardware Protection (Remove or Mask)
notes: Remove or tape/bag window hardware (locks, latches, crank operators). ~3 min per hardware group. Removal slightly slower but produces cleaner finish.

name: Wall Masking Around Window
notes: Tape + paper masking around window perimeter to protect wall. ~24 sec per LF. Spray method always, brush method only when walls SS_PAINTED_*.

name: Sill/Stool Protection
notes: Tape sill/stool edge to protect finished surface. ~18 sec per LF. Simpler than wall masking (tape-only, no paper). Only when stool is SS_PAINTED_* and method is spray.

name: Sand Bare Wood Windows
notes: Sand bare wood window frame, sash, muntins, extension jamb with 150-220 grit sequence. Rate for medium double-hung. Complex 3D assembly (profiles, edges, recesses) is slower than flat linear trim. Per Window_Systems_Doctrine Section 3.2.

name: Scuff Sand Factory Primer
notes: Light scuff sand factory primer with 220 grit for adhesion. ~5 min per medium window. Not removing material — creating tooth. Same pace at all tiers (adhesion prep is not tiered). Per research EST-007.

name: Degrease Metal Windows
notes: Thorough degreasing with alkaline cleaner (BC-7000 or equivalent). ~4 min per medium window. Apply cleaner, scrub, rinse, verify water-break test. Per Window_Systems_Doctrine Section 6.1.

name: Chemical Etch / Abrasion — Aluminum
notes: Chemical etch or mechanical abrasion of aluminum surfaces. ~6 min per medium window. Scotch-Brite pad for mechanical abrasion, or apply/dwell/rinse for chemical etch. Per Window_Systems_Doctrine Section 6.2.

name: Rust Assessment and Treatment — Steel
notes: Rust assessment per SSPC standards, mechanical/chemical treatment, rust converter application. Rate varies by condition severity (surface vs scale vs pitting) AND quality tier (thoroughness increases). Per Window_Systems_Doctrine Section 6.3.

name: Clean Prep Dust and Debris
notes: Tack cloth wipe all prepped window surfaces. ~2 min per medium window. Quick pass — same pace at all tiers. Complete dust removal is binary.

name: Brush Primer Coat
notes: Brush primer on all window surfaces (frame, sash, muntins, extension jamb) using 1.5" and 2-2.5" angled sash brushes. ~10 min per medium DH. Slower than finish coat due to bare substrate absorption and careful coverage. Per research EST-007 (~0.4-0.6 hrs/EA total primer pathway, ~0.15 hrs application).

name: Spray Primer Coat
notes: Spray primer via airless (310-411 tip). ~4 min per medium window. ~2.5x faster than brush. Requires additional masking already set up in setup module.

name: Brush Finish Coat 1
notes: Brush finish coat 1 on all window surfaces using 1.5" (sash, muntins) and 2-2.5" (frame, jamb) angled sash brushes. ~17 min per medium DH. Slowest task in the spec — precision detail work on 3D assembly. Coat 1 slower than coat 2 (surface absorption, establishing coverage). Derived from Window_Systems_Doctrine Section 8.3 decomposition.

name: Spray Finish Coat 1
notes: Airless spray finish coat 1 (310-411 tip). ~7.5 min per medium window. ~2.3x faster than brush. Coat 1 slower than coat 2 (establishing coverage). Consistent distance and speed for uniform mil thickness. 20-40% material waste from overspray.

name: Inspect Coat (Interstage)
notes: Visual inspection of applied coat on all window surfaces. Slower per EA than trim inspection per LF because window is a complex 3D assembly (frame, sash, muntins, jamb — all surfaces must be checked). Rates derived from trim inspection rates adapted for EA-based window geometry.

name: Sand Between Coats
notes: Between-coat sanding with rigid sanding block (FFD 15.4.1). Window sanding is slower per unit than trim sanding — 3D assembly with profiles, recesses, and muntin edges requires careful technique vs flat linear trim. Research RF-011.

name: Patch/Repair Defects (Interstage)
notes: Spot fill/patch defects found during interstage inspection. Walk rate — most windows need minimal patching in NC. Scope increases at higher tiers.

name: Spot Coat Patched Areas
notes: Apply spot coat over patched/repaired areas. Walk rate — scope proportional to patch scope. Most windows need minimal spot coating in NC.

name: Clean Sanding Dust (Interstage)
notes: Tack cloth wipe all sanded window surfaces between coats. ~2 min per medium window. Same pace at all tiers — complete dust removal is binary.

name: Brush Finish Coat 2
notes: Brush finish coat 2. ~15 min per medium DH. Faster than coat 1 — consistent substrate, no absorption. Same application philosophy: apply, tip once, walk away. Also used for coat 3 at QT5 brush/roll. Per research EST-001.

name: Spray Finish Coat 2
notes: Airless spray finish coat 2. ~6 min per medium window. Faster than coat 1 — consistent substrate.

name: Final Window Inspection
notes: Final quality check of all painted window surfaces. Slower than interstage inspect because final inspection is more thorough — verify sheen consistency, coverage uniformity, sash position (ajar), glass edge quality.

name: Touch-Up Defects (Final)
notes: Touch-up defects found during final inspection. Walk rate with spot work. QT5 may require full coat over repair areas to equalize sheen.

name: Glass Scraping / Cleanup
notes: Occurs AFTER full cure (3-7 days for enamels). May happen on a different day than other cleanup tasks.

name: Reinstall Window Hardware
notes: Reinstall removed hardware (locks, latches, crank operators) or remove masking from in-place hardware. ~3 min per window. Verify operation after reinstall.

name: Protection Teardown

Wall/sill/hardware masking teardown bundled into rate. Glass masking removed during glass scrape task (not this task).
